findings.title: A pause recreated by refusal
findings.claim: As a bounded narrative analogy, the attenuation named by the focus interval can be recreated after address when refusal of movement turns active prophetic speech into a long reception-side pause.
findings.mechanism: The focus fatrah occurrence at 5:19:9:1 meets the supplied later occurrences of imagined endless duration, continuance, deliberate sitting, and a measured forty-year delay; the sequence shifts the pause from chronology alone toward a pause produced in reception while preserving the focus's ordinary interval sense.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how an interval between messages and a later refusal to move mirror one another as different kinds of attenuation: one between sendings, one in the audience's response.
findings.containment: The focus phrase remains a chronological period between messengers. This is an exploratory analogy about how reception can reproduce attenuation, not a redefinition of the grammatical phrase as audience-caused; the source is legacy_unbound and its trace explicitly remains exploratory.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus and context coordinates support a coherent analogy, but the HFT confidence is exploratory, the reader identity is legacy_unbound, and all non-focus branch descriptors are unresolved.
